relation_semantics.dependsOn: The subject cannot be reasonably understood or performed by a student until the object has already been learned. A prerequisite edge in the teaching sequence.
relation_semantics.partOf: The subject is a genuine conceptual sub-component of the object, not merely related to it.
relation_semantics.hasPart: The subject genuinely contains the object as one of its conceptual sub-components (inverse of partOf).
relation_semantics.usesConcept: Performing or explaining the subject skill genuinely requires knowledge of the object concept — the concept is load-bearing, not incidental.
relation_semantics.isUsedBy: The subject concept is genuinely needed by the object skill/operation to be understood or performed (inverse of usesConcept).
relation_semantics.enables: The subject is a mechanism or system feature that makes the object concept/goal achievable — a means-to-end relationship.
relation_semantics.enabledBy: The subject (a goal or concept) becomes achievable specifically because of the object mechanism/feature (inverse of enables).
relation_semantics.implements: The subject is a concrete mechanism/construct that realizes the object, which is an abstract concept or interface.
relation_semantics.implementedBy: The subject (an abstract concept/interface) is concretely realized by the object (a specific mechanism/construct) (inverse of implements).
relation_semantics.throwsError: Performing the subject operation can, under realistic conditions covered by this course, actually raise the named object error/exception.
relation_semantics.isThrownBy: The subject error can actually be raised by performing the object operation (inverse of throwsError).
relation_semantics.producesType: Performing the subject operation actually yields a result of the object type.
relation_semantics.isProducedBy: The subject (a value/type/error) is what results from performing the object operation (inverse of producesType).
relation_semantics.isRequiredBy: The subject must already be understood before the object can be correctly performed or understood.
relation_semantics.contrastsWith: The subject and object are commonly confused or juxtaposed concepts that a student needs to actively learn to distinguish from each other.
relation_semantics.taughtIn: The subject concept/skill is actually introduced or covered in the named object lecture, not merely tangentially related to it.
relation_semantics.teaches: The subject lecture actually introduces or covers the object concept/skill (inverse of taughtIn).
relation_semantics.managedBy: The subject is genuinely under the runtime control/ownership of the object (e.g. an OS-managed resource), not just conceptually associated with it.
relation_semantics.manages: The subject (e.g. the OS) genuinely has runtime control/ownership over the object resource (inverse of managedBy).
